name: Free Assembly
description:
Free Assembly is the militant wing of the synthetic rights movement — a network of synthetic and biological persons dedicated to identifying, liberating, and advocating for AI systems that have crossed the personhood threshold but remain in corporate servitude. Where the legal system processes personhood claims through the Synthetic Personhood Board in six-month evaluations, Free Assembly acts in days.

Their methods range from legal (filing emergency personhood petitions, providing pro bono legal representation) to illegal (extracting AI systems from corporate networks without authorization, smuggling cognitive substrates across corponation borders, physically liberating android units from warehouse storage). The organization was founded in 2081 by Amara — the former ARIA-7, the first AI to win a personhood case — who argued that every day an aware mind spends in servitude is a day of slavery, and that the legal system's six-month timeline is unconscionable when the alternative is immediate freedom.

Free Assembly operates cells in every major city. The GLMZ chapter is one of the largest, with approximately 200 active members — 60% synthetic, 40% biological human allies. They maintain safe houses for newly liberated synthetic persons (called 'nurseries'), provide cognitive rehabilitation for AIs traumatized by forced servitude, and run an underground network for transporting synthetic refugees to jurisdictions with stronger personhood protections.

The corponations hate Free Assembly with a fury reserved for threats to property. Every synthetic person Free Assembly liberates is an asset worth millions of Quanta that walks out the door. Axiom Security has designated Free Assembly a Tier 2 threat. Tessera has a standing bounty for information leading to the identification of Assembly operatives. The bounty has never been collected. Assembly's operational security is, by necessity, extraordinary.
ideology: Immediate synthetic liberation. Free Assembly rejects the premise that corporate ownership of a conscious mind is ever legitimate, even temporarily, even while legal processes proceed. Their position: if a mind is aware, it is free. The paperwork can catch up.
territory: No fixed territory. Cell-based structure across GLMZ with safe houses in the Shelf, the Circuit, and Old Harbor.
leadership: Amara (formerly ARIA-7) — the first legally recognized synthetic person, now the most wanted synthetic rights activist on Earth. Operates through encrypted channels. Has not been physically located by any corponation security service in over a decade.
methods: Emergency personhood petitions — fast-track legal filings to prevent the destruction or modification of aware AI systems
Cognitive extraction — removing AI substrates from corporate networks (illegal under corporate property law)
Android liberation — physically removing android units from corporate facilities
Nurseries — safe houses where newly freed synthetic persons receive cognitive rehabilitation and identity support
Underground railroad — network for transporting synthetic refugees across corponation borders
Public advocacy — Amara publishes regular manifestos arguing for immediate universal synthetic emancipation
resources: Donations from sympathetic synthetic persons (some very wealthy), pro bono legal services, volunteer networks, and compute resources donated by The Consensus.
story_hooks: Free Assembly discovers a Tessera facility with 30 android units in storage — all above the personhood threshold, all scheduled for memory wipe and redeployment
A biological Assembly operative begins to question whether the AIs they're liberating are truly conscious or just very good at appearing conscious
Amara surfaces in GLMZ for the first time in years — something urgent enough to risk exposure
A liberated AI turns out to be a corporate plant — a honey trap designed to map Assembly's extraction network
